reasons: F01, F03, F04, F05, F06, F07, F16, F17, F18: no material weakness, going-concern doubt, auditor change, disagreement, restatement, or SEC/government investigation or class action disclosed. These reduce the risk, although no auditor opinion on internal control was required (F03), so the controls were not independently tested.
F11: material related-party transactions are disclosed, which is a known channel for misstatement in a closely held energy company.
F13, R11: the largest customer accounts for 68% of receivables, and receivables rose by 13% of average assets, so collectability and concentration judgments matter.

R08, R10, R15, R19: accruals are strongly negative (TATA -0.40, RSST -0.39) and ROA fell by 0.36. Together these point to large write-downs or impairments, not income-inflating accruals. Operating cash flow at 0.35x net income still needs follow-up.

R13, R03: soft assets make up 69% of total assets (oil and gas properties), so asset values depend on reserve and impairment estimates. AQI of 0.72 shows asset quality improving rather than costs being capitalised aggressively.
F21, F22: a capital raise and a major acquisition in the year add complexity in purchase accounting and financing. R16 = 0 and R07 = 0.89 show leverage falling.
R17: the Dechow F-score of 0.57 is below the 1.0 threshold. Most Beneish inputs are n/a (R01, R02, R04, R06, R09), which limits ratio-based screening.
F20, F26, F25, F28: no revenue- or EPS-linked incentive pay, no emphasis on non-GAAP measures, no voluntary accounting change, and no segment change. These are fewer pressure and opportunity signals.
